out: Prison Link Cymru reports that 1,099 ex-offenders were referred to the charity in 2015-16, with some living rough for up to a year before finding accommodation. The organization argues that investment in housing is cheaper than jailing homeless repeat offenders, noting that the Welsh Government has removed priority status for prison leavers under recent Housing Act changes. While women generally fare better due to considerations like children and domestic violence, men often struggle with issues like PTSD and drug dependency being deprioritized, with charity workers describing the need for accommodation as "chronic

Police searched properties in Waterfront Park and Colonsay View, recovering three firearms, ammunition, and a five-figure sum of money. A 26-year-old man was subsequently charged and appeared at Edinburgh Sheriff Court on Thursday.

Four individuals, including Jordan Hill, Brittany Covington, Tesfaye Cooper, and Tanishia Covington, appeared in court charged with hate crimes and aggravated kidnapping and battery. Prosecutors allege the victim, an 18-year-old white man with disabilities, was tortured in a van and a house, forced to drink toilet water, and subjected to racist and derogatory slurs during a Facebook Live broadcast. The suspects were denied bail, with the judge questioning their "sense of decency" as prosecutors detailed the severity of the alleged abuse.

Former Arsenal goalkeeper David James has left West Bromwich Albion after four years, having served as youth academy director since 2000 and director of football since 2003. He played a key role in the club's promotion to the Premier League in 2006 and 2012.

A modified "fasting-mimicking diet" has been shown to reverse diabetes symptoms in mice by regenerating insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas. The diet, which cycles between periods of fasting and normal eating, appears to trigger developmental reprogramming in the organ. While the findings are promising for both type 1 and type 2 diabetes, researchers caution against unsupervised crash dieting.

Essilor and Luxottica, the world's top lens and frame manufacturers respectively, are planning a merger to create EssilorLuxottica, a dominant industry player. While the companies argue the deal will generate innovation and benefit customers, industry experts warn it could reduce consumer choice and squeeze out smaller competitors. The merger would give the new entity significant control over the global eyewear market, potentially creating a "stranglehold" on high-end glasses.

Former Olympic silver medallist Houvenaghel has accused British Cycling of "ageism" and "zero regard" for athlete welfare, joining a growing list of high-profile cyclists criticizing the organization's culture. She claimed to feel "vindicated" by a leaked report detailing systemic failures, stating the body prioritized winning medals over the wellbeing of staff and athletes. British Cycling has since acknowledged past failings and implemented a 39-point action plan to address the issues, though Houvenaghel's comments highlight a deep-seated "win-at-all-costs" culture that has driven

Kareem Badr and two friends took over a struggling Austin improv theater in 2009, betting on their passion to bail out the "sinking ship" despite lacking business experience. Their strategy of breaking down complex problems into manageable parts helped the club survive the 2008 recession and grow, allowing Badr to eventually quit his day job and expand the venue. Today, the Hideout benefits from a national comedy boom, with the industry expected to reach $344.6 million by 2020, driven by stand-up's rising popularity among younger

Ofcom abandoned plans to break up BT over "practical obstacles," primarily citing complications with the company's £40 billion pension scheme and land deals. While BT's shares rose on the news, the regulator signaled it would enforce structural changes through new board rules rather than a full split.

Brendan Rodgers is preparing for his second Old Man derby with Rangers, aiming to replicate the 5-1 league victory his team achieved at Celtic Park last month. He emphasized that while the previous Scottish Cup semi-final defeat at Hampden is in the past, his current squad has a different mentality and is focused on imposing their style of play to secure a win. Rodgers views the League Cup final as a priority and a chance to win silverware, rather than a stepping stone to a domestic treble.

Facing an £8m cut in government subsidy, Queen's University Belfast plans to reduce undergraduate places by 1,010 over three years, potentially impacting staff and course viability. The Education Minister warned students may leave Northern Ireland for other UK universities, while the vice-chancellor cautioned the cuts could damage the institution's reputation and the local economy.

East Sussex NHS Trust mistakenly sent cancer information leaflets to approximately 850 patients who were not referred for urgent appointments due to an external printing company's error in March. The trust has since apologized to those affected and confirmed the issue has been resolved.

Labour has pledged not to "frustrate Brexit" despite internal rebellion, with shadow ministers defying the whip to demand amendments on the final deal and EU nationals' rights. While frontbenchers face potential resignation if they defy the whip again, party leader Jeremy Corbyn has indicated he expects rebels like Diane Abbott to fall into line, insisting the party will ultimately support the bill to respect the referendum result.

The National League club sold midfielder O'Kane to Bournemouth in 2012 with a 15% sell-on clause, but the current manager says he won't receive any of the proceeds due to the club's financial struggles. The Gulls are currently seeking new ownership after being forced to close their academy and reduce their playing budget following the departure of former owner Thea Bristow.

Iwan Wyn Lewis, a 36-year-old patient at Ysbyty Gwynedd, died by suicide in the Menai Strait shortly after telling staff he was going to the shop. An inquest heard that a police visit to discuss his bail arrangements, which his psychiatrist believed added to his distress, occurred the day before his death. Dr. Olufemi Adebajo stated that the officer's visit was "likely" to have contributed to Mr. Lewis's agitation, despite the doctor previously considering him low suicide risk.

The 33-year-old forward has made only two appearances for Leicester City this season after signing a new one-year deal in the summer. He joined the 13th-placed Owls ahead of their Championship match against Norwich City, having previously scored three goals in 23 games for his parent club last season.

US scientists are rushing to copy climate data onto external servers, fearing the Trump administration will restrict access to research. Dr. Waleed Abdalati warns that such data, paid for by taxpayers, is essential, while others, like Prof. Robert Paterson, advise preparing for potential censorship by creating "mirror sites."

The Specials have announced the death of their beloved drummer, John 'Brad' Bradbury, who passed away at age 59. The band confirmed the sad news via social media, noting that Brad was the "powerhouse" behind their iconic Two Tone sound and a key figure in their reunion tours. Tributes have poured in from fellow musicians, including Billy Bragg and Pete Waterman, highlighting his significant impact on the ska and reggae scene.

Tiger Woods missed the cut at the Farmers Insurance Open after carding a level-par 72 in the second round, following a first-round 76. Joining him in missing the cut were world number one Jason Day and US Open champion Dustin Johnson. Despite the early exit, Woods noted his game was improving, stating he hit the ball much better on the second day.

Former Manchester United forward Dwight Yorke has revealed he is not fit to travel to Barcelona for a legends game due to complications from kidney failure, crediting his 28-year-old nephew Alexander with a "noble" donor transplant. While Yorke has made significant physical improvements since his 2015 illness, he remains some way off full fitness and is focusing on recovery ahead of potentially playing in a similar match next year. He also echoed Alan Shearer's view that English clubs are currently a long way off challenging Europe's elite for the Champions League.

Pakistan has lifted its five-year ban on YouTube after Google launched a Pakistan-specific version of the platform, allowing the telecoms regulator to request the removal of offending content. While many young Pakistanis have welcomed the return of the site, activists are demanding greater transparency regarding the terms of the agreement between the government and Google.

26-year-old Benjamin has been ruled out for the remainder of the season after sustaining an injury during last week's win over Exeter. Director of rugby Richard Cockerill confirmed the injury is not serious, with the player expected to make a full recovery in eight to ten weeks. Meanwhile, scrum-half Sam Harrison has signed a new contract, though the length of the deal remains undisclosed.

Great Britain's Owain Doull helped his team set a world record to win Olympic gold in the men's team pursuit, marking Wales' first cycling gold since 2008 and Great Britain's third consecutive title in the event. Doull, who emulated his idol Geraint Thomas, described the victory as "surreal" and "dreamlike," crediting the experience of his teammates, including Bradley Wiggins, who became the first Briton to win eight Olympic medals. This win ended a 36-year drought for Welsh Olympic cycling gold and secured Doull's personal redemption

The death toll has doubled over two days as officials recovered over 100 bodies following receding floodwaters, affecting 450,000 people in one state. Millions across 20 Indian states have been impacted by this year's monsoon rains, with the north-eastern state of Assam seeing dozens killed and hundreds of thousands displaced. The government has pledged aid and Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to visit Assam on Tuesday to seek a "permanent solution" to the annual flooding.

Two Scottish enthusiasts, Bridget and Jonathan Reid, married at the Nevis Range ski resort, donning full Highland dress including kilts and a white wedding dress before skiing down the mountain. The ceremony, officiated by Halde Pottinger at the top of Easy Gully, was made possible by recent snowfall and marked the couple's first date six years prior, which was also a skiing trip.

Hong Kong regulators fined RBS £1.5 million after a former trader, Shirlina Tsang, was convicted of fraud for falsifying emerging markets trade records. The Securities and Futures Commission cited "seriously inadequate" controls and "significant weaknesses" in management, but reduced the penalty due to the bank's swift reporting of the 2011 illegal trades. This fine is notably smaller than RBS's recent penalties of £320m for rate rigging and £60m for sanctions violations.

At the Baftas backstage, Emma Stone joked that Mia from *La La Land* could win an Oscar, while Tom Holland celebrated his Rising Star win despite sore legs from Spider-Man poses. Viola Davis passionately defended Meryl Streep against Donald Trump's "overrated" comments, and Casey Affleck praised her for speaking out, noting the importance of using these platforms to address important issues.

Andy Murray's 2017 season has been marked by a decline in form and persistent injury concerns, highlighted by his first-round defeat at Queen's Club. While he remains a two-time Wimbledon champion and Olympic gold medalist, his current struggles with movement and serve suggest he may not be at his peak heading into the tournament. Although he aims for a 10th consecutive quarter-final, his recent results and physical issues cast doubt on his ability to challenge for the title.

Mandla Hlatshwayo was shot dead in Soweto after confronting men who had robbed women of their phones. The suspects were found with drugs and an unlicensed gun, and police are currently questioning them regarding the incident.

Witnesses reported hearing a gun fired near Anfield Road Primary School around 9:00 AM, prompting a lockdown of nearby schools. Police are investigating the incident as targeted, with a search ongoing for a white man in a grey hooded top who fled the scene in a dark-colored car.

Ennis-Hill sits in third place after the first day of the heptathlon with 3,928 points, but remains in contention for Olympic qualification. She recorded a strong long jump but a disappointing javelin throw, leaving her with 5,544 points going into the final 800m. With a top-12 finish and a score of 6,075, she could secure a spot at this summer's World Championships.

Manor's operating company entered administration on January 6, and FRP Advisory failed to find a buyer, leading to the team's trading cessation and staff redundancies. Although a buyer could still purchase the team's remnants, the collapse makes it highly unlikely Manor will compete in the season-opening Australian Grand Prix on March 26. The collapse leaves 10 teams and 20 cars on the grid, marking the end of a seven-year struggle for the squad that started as Virgin Racing in 2010.

The Northern Ireland Assembly election on March 2nd will see 228 candidates compete for 90 seats, a decrease from the previous 108. The DUP is fielding the most candidates (38), while the constituency of Newry and Armagh has the fewest with only nine candidates on the ballot.

The article advises that while the pound has fallen about 18% against the dollar since the Brexit vote due to differing economic outlooks, the exchange rate remains volatile due to events like the US election. It suggests that travelers avoid last-minute airport exchanges and instead shop online or split their currency purchases to mitigate risk and get the best rate.

More than 300 people entered the Alternative Model of the Year competition, with 19-year-old Newcastle University student Zoe Waters taking the title. Waters, who describes her style as "crazy" and non-conformist, said she never imagined she could be a model due to her height, but now plans to pursue a career in the industry. The event, organized to celebrate subcultures and challenge prejudice, was held at Northumbria University in Newcastle.

The National Museum of the Royal Navy plans to relocate the Yomper statue from the Royal Marines Museum in Eastney to Portsmouth Historic Dockyard as part of a £13 million project. However, campaigners and local officials argue the statue, unveiled by Lady Thatcher in 1992, should remain at Eastney as a dedicated Falklands War memorial. An online petition with over 1,800 signatures opposes the move, stating the statue's scale and meaning are best appreciated in its current location.

A suspect identified only as BM appeared at the Old Bailey accused of breaching a Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measure (TPim) by failing to report to a police station and contact a monitoring company in January. The Home Office has refused to comment on the case, which is believed to be the first alleged breach of the measure since it replaced control orders in 2012.

Former Sussex cricketer Seamer Anyon has been appointed as the new coach of the men's second XI, taking over from Charlotte Burton. He will also coach the women's under-19 and under-21 sides, citing the rapidly growing women's game as a key motivation for the role. Additionally, Alexia Walker has been given expanded responsibilities to coach the senior women's side alongside her existing duties with the under-17 and under-21 teams.

The 23-year-old younger brother of Sunderland's Wes Brown is available for Bury's League One opener after being on trial with the Shakers. Having previously played for clubs including Bradford and Watford, he will make his Bury debut in their season opener at Doncaster on Saturday.

The latest live-action "Cinderella" directed by Kenneth Branagh has become a box office success, grossing $70 million in its U.S. opening weekend. The film distinguishes itself by remaining largely faithful to the classic animated original, with Lily James starring as a proactive Cinderella who makes active choices rather than passively waiting for rescue. Despite critics noting its traditional "preserved-in-amber" romance, the cast and crew argue that the film's commitment to the source material is precisely what resonates with modern audiences.

Russia was banned from Eurovision 2017 after singer Julia Samoilova performed in Crimea in 2015, which Ukraine considers an illegal annexation. The European Broadcasting Union offered Russia a satellite performance, but Moscow declined, viewing the ban as a political provocation. The dispute highlights the ongoing tension between Kiev and Moscow, with Ukraine viewing the inclusion as a violation of its sovereignty laws.

Alex McKechnie, a teenager working in Liverpool at the time, witnessed The Beatles' early performances at the Cavern Club in 1961. He recalls the cramped, electric atmosphere of the basement venue, where the band distinguished themselves by playing Chuck Berry riffs and rebellious, out-of-step dance moves. McKechnie emphasizes that the Beatles' charm, harmonies, and deliberate defiance of audience expectations made them the "epitome of rebellion" in Liverpool.

South Africa is moving toward introducing a national minimum wage to combat poverty, though critics argue it is too low and could increase unemployment. The government aims to finalize the rate within two years, but labor unions and opposition parties have criticized the proposal as favoring businesses over workers.

Concern is mounting over a power struggle in Addis Ababa that could destabilize the Horn of Africa, particularly as Somalia's political transition remains fragile and a South Sudan-Sudan standoff risks further conflict. Meles Zenawi is remembered as a complex, charismatic revolutionary who transformed Ethiopia's economy and regional influence, but his legacy is marred by authoritarianism, stalled political reform, and deepening poverty despite his promises of modernization and federalism.

Australia took a 1-0 lead in the series after rain and poor light halted play on day two of the second Test at the MCG. Despite only 50.5 overs being bowled, Australia claimed regular wickets, including the dismissals of Younus Khan and Misbah-ul-Haq, to leave Pakistan struggling at 111 for 5. Azhar Ali's half-century was the highlight for the visitors before the match was called off.

In a Leith Walk by-election, the SNP's John Lewis Ritchie won the first seat with 2,290 first-preference votes, while Labour's Marion Donaldson secured the second seat after transfers. The SNP also retained the Midlothian West seat with Kelly Parry winning, as both contests were triggered by SNP and Green councillors stepping down.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated that Russia will continue supporting Syrian forces and urged the US to separate moderate rebels from "terrorists," warning that a refusal to cooperate would benefit extremists. Despite the collapse of the latest truce and intensifying attacks on Aleppo, Russia remains interested in diplomatic talks, with US and Turkish officials also reviewing options to restart negotiations and establish a new ceasefire.

Hooker Hughes and flanker Evans, both 19 or 20, have been selected in Wales' squad for the Junior World Championship in Manchester this June. The pair enjoyed successful Six Nations campaigns and will aim to build on that momentum in Pool A, which also features Ireland, Georgia, and New Zealand.

The article details the escalating tension between the US and Russia following the Obama administration's imposition of new sanctions. Russian officials, including President Medvedev and Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova, have harshly criticized the move as "vindictive" and an attempt to undermine Donald Trump's incoming presidency. The sanctions are framed by the US as a response to alleged Russian interference in the election and harassment of US personnel, while Russia denies the accusations and views the actions as an effort to sabotage US-Russian relations.

Jeremy Corbyn is proposing to abolish university tuition fees in England, positioning it as a fundamental right rather than a marketised cost, and framing it as the starkest policy choice in two decades to appeal to younger voters. Labour has costed the plan—including the reintroduction of maintenance grants—at £11.2 billion per year, funded by tax changes, though independent forecasters suggest the true cost could be lower once loan write-offs are considered. However, the policy faces warnings that removing fees could restrict university expansion and place limits on student numbers, potentially undermining the very

Eleven people were killed when a vintage Hawker Hunter jet crashed into traffic on the A27 on 22 August. West Sussex Fire and Rescue Service described the recovery as "extremely challenging," and while police have finished their scene work, investigations into the cause continue.

Dan Coats and Admiral Mike Rogers testified before the Senate Intelligence Committee, declining to discuss their private conversations with President Trump regarding the Russia investigation. Both officials refused to share details in an open hearing, citing the need to protect sensitive information. Their testimony was seen as a letdown compared to former FBI Director James Comey's upcoming appearance, as they largely avoided addressing the president's alleged attempts to influence the probe.

President Obama hosted a private party for 500 guests, including celebrities like Prince and Stevie Wonder, which the White House press secretary confirmed was paid for by the Obamas themselves. The event featured performances by the musicians and was attended by figures such as Al Sharpton, Angela Bassett, and Tyler Perry.

These six rural roads in Northern Ireland have been officially renamed to remove the word "Black," which is a racial slur. The changes apply to roads in Loughgall, Poyntzpass, Dundonald, Hillsborough, Rathfriland, and Derrygonnelly.

In the BBC One documentary "Doctor in the House," Dr. Rangan Chatterjee helped 34-year-old Emma Gleeson manage her severe anxiety and panic attacks by transforming her diet. By replacing processed foods and sugary drinks with fresh, whole foods and reducing her alcohol intake, Emma experienced significant improvements in her mood, energy, and mental clarity. This case highlights the growing evidence that nutrition plays a crucial role in mental health, yet remains largely overlooked in standard medical care.

The Alabama Securities Commission closed its investigation into Harper Lee's capacity to consent to publishing "Go Set a Watchman," concluding she was mentally competent. The commission's director stated Lee satisfactorily answered their questions, dispelling concerns she was manipulated. The 88-year-old author's first new book in decades will now be released following the investigation's conclusion.

The U.S. has suspended bilateral talks with Russia over Syria, accusing Moscow and the Syrian government of intensifying attacks on civilians and failing to uphold ceasefire commitments. In response, Russia expressed regret, blaming the U.S. for the truce's collapse and warning that the suspension could hinder counter-terrorism coordination. The move follows a week of heavy bombardment in Aleppo, including strikes on a hospital and a humanitarian aid convoy, which have trapped hundreds of thousands of people in the rebel-held east.

Sadiq Khan won the London mayoral election, becoming the city's first Muslim mayor and defeating Zac Goldsmith in a race defined by debates over immigration and social mobility. His victory was celebrated globally as a rebuke to rising right-wing politics and a testament to London's diversity, with international leaders hailing it as a historic moment for immigrant integration.

Parishioners at St Paul's in Shipley created a viral Facebook video to recruit a new vicar after traditional methods failed, attracting over 30,000 views and media attention. The children, with the help of the church's musical director, wrote a song detailing the ideal candidate's qualities, ranging from a "cheery disposition" and a love of Harry Potter to keeping the church tidy. The new vicar, Henriette Howarth, is set to take up the post next week.

Kevin De Bruyne suffered a significant injury during Manchester City's win over Everton, with initial reports suggesting a six-week absence now extended to around 10 weeks. The absence will see him miss crucial fixtures including the League Cup final and the Champions League last-16 tie, leaving City without their second-top scorer for a substantial period.

A 27-year-old Swiss man set fire to a train and stabbed passengers near Salez station on Saturday, injuring six people, including a six-year-old child in serious condition. The attacker died from his injuries, and police have stated there is currently no indication of a political or terrorist motive.

A Flybe passenger plane came within 2 miles of a drone near Cornwall Airport Newquay on Tuesday, prompting a police search that failed to find the operator. Devon and Cornwall Police have called the incident "incredibly concerning," emphasizing the reckless nature of flying drones in active airspace without clearance.

A grey seal was found tangled in heavy netting at Cruden Bay, and the Scottish SPCA rescued it, cutting the netting away at their Drumoak centre. Insp. John Carle noted the net was the largest he had ever seen and that the seal was successfully released back into the water without injury.

The National Library of Scotland has catalogued the archive of travel writer and war hero Sir Patrick Leigh Fermor, revealing letters from Prince Charles and Truman Capote, along with his prized 1933 trek notebooks that inspired his famous trilogy. The collection, which took a year to organize, highlights his daring WWII exploits in Crete and includes unpublished manuscripts and sketches. The library is now digitizing the archive and planning exhibitions to make it more widely accessible.

Mr. Roache was elected as the new general secretary of the GMB union, securing 56.7% of the vote against Paul McCarthy. He succeeds Paul Kenny, who is stepping down after nearly a decade, and pledged to lead a "21st Century union" fighting for members' rights.

Laura Marling is set to appear on the new series of *Later... with Jools Holland*, marking a significant moment given her well-documented struggles with stage fright and anxiety. Despite her terror of live television, she views the invitation as a huge honor, calling host Jools Holland a "genuine champion" who personally reached out to discuss her new music. She will perform tracks from her upcoming album *The Dreaming Room*, aiming to showcase a rawer, darker sound that reflects her current artistic growth.

Jonas Gutierrez revealed he was "born again" after overcoming testicular cancer and chemotherapy, making his return to Newcastle's first team in March. The Argentine forward, whose contract expires this summer, is focused on securing regular playing time and is determined to prove he can still compete in the Premier League.

Exeter City reported a £1.642m profit for 2014-15, primarily driven by the sale of Matt Grimes to Swansea City for a club-record £1.75m. The financial success came despite the club facing a transfer embargo and an emergency loan to cover wages earlier that year. The club is now planning to redevelop St James Park using the transfer funds to strengthen its infrastructure.

Abdullah Hayayei, a UAE para-athlete, died after a training cage collapsed on his head at Newham Leisure Centre ahead of the World Para-athletics Championships. The incident is under investigation by police and the Health and Safety Executive, with tributes paid as his team vows to compete in his memory.

The article reports that Scottish businesses are optimistic about 2017, with growth in manufacturing and retail despite concerns over rising prices and skill shortages. While the economy shows positive signs in new orders and visitor numbers, firms face challenges from inflation and cash flow issues, though exporters continue to report healthy trade growth.

The Royal Courts of Justice are currently hearing the first public examination of undercover policing, following allegations of human rights abuses and relationships with women using false identities. Lawyers have uncovered over 80 potential miscarriages of justice, with victims like "Jacqui" and "Alison" describing the profound personal devastation caused by officers who infiltrated groups under false pretenses. The inquiry aims to establish the truth and make recommendations for the future deployment of undercover officers, though victims demand accountability and justice for the decades-long deception.

The All Blacks overcame a five-point half-time deficit and a first-half red card to defeat South Africa 20-18 in a gripping World Cup quarter-final. Despite a dominant Springbok defense and a tense finale, New Zealand held their two-point lead for the final 12 minutes to advance to the semi-finals. This victory marks the All Blacks as strong favorites to retain the Webb Ellis Trophy, despite the match lacking the free-flowing attack seen earlier in the tournament.

The National Trust is using ground-penetrating radar to investigate the internal structure of the Wellington Monument on the Blackdown Hills, which has been fenced off since 2005 due to falling stonework. The survey aims to identify voids in the masonry and create a computer model to inform a more effective repair approach for the 174ft tower, which has required renovations every decade due to weather damage and lightning strikes.

Inditex, the parent company of Zara, reported an 8% increase in net earnings to €1.26bn and an 11% rise in sales to €10.5bn for the first half of the year. The retailer expanded its online presence to 40 countries and opened 83 new stores across 38 nations, reinforcing its strategy of integrating technology and physical retail to drive growth despite a challenging European market.

Lady Gaga is preparing a "spectacular" Super Bowl performance with a massive production, aiming to live up to legendary halftime shows like Prince's 2007 set. The article highlights iconic past moments, from Michael Jackson's 90-second pause to Bruce Springsteen's infamous "crotch slam," while noting Beyoncé's politically charged 2016 performance and Diana Ross's dramatic helicopter exit.

A new BBC One documentary, "The Betrayed Girls," revisits the 2012 Rochdale grooming case, highlighting that victims like Laura still face harassment and feel unheard. Former chief crown prosecutor Nazir Afzal warns that while awareness has improved, many victims nationally are still not being consistently listened to, and some are told cases are "too difficult" to prosecute. GMP and local councils maintain they are committed to tackling the issue, but Afzal stresses the need for better collaboration between agencies to protect vulnerable children.

A burst pipe caused severe flooding at the Victoria Centre store on Tuesday night, damaging stock and forcing the closure of the top floor. Managers had hoped for a weekend reopening, but the store remains closed "until further notice" while staff work to clear the water and repair the damage.

A flood of automated comments, likely using stolen personal data, has inundated the FCC's net neutrality proceeding, creating a "bot army" that mimics genuine public outrage. Experts suggest this artificial surge is designed to obscure real public opinion, potentially misleading the FCC into believing opposition is less widespread than it actually is. The activity follows comedian John Oliver's call to action and coincides with a DDoS attack that disabled the FCC's comment system earlier this month.

Sale Sharks have moved home games back to Friday nights and restructured their board following Simon Orange's takeover. New chairman Mike Cotton aims to improve the fan experience and infrastructure, emphasizing that the coaching staff and board will work closely together to build a competitive north of England club.

Moana dominated the Thanksgiving box office with an $81.1 million debut, becoming the second-highest Thanksgiving opening ever behind Frozen. However, the film faced criticism for cultural appropriation, leading Disney to withdraw a Maui costume labeled as "brownface." Meanwhile, "Allied" and "Rules Don't Apply" struggled, taking $18 million and $2.2 million respectively.

The third seed defeated the American wildcard 6-3, 6-1 in just over an hour to reach the quarter-finals. She will face China's Saisai Zheng on Friday after Zheng beat Alize Cornet in the previous round.

Two men were taken to hospital after being injured in an attack on Linn Road in the town at around 2:05 PM on Sunday. Police are appealing for witnesses to come forward with information about the incident.

Researchers investigating the origin of the Ebola outbreak in Guinea traced the index case, Emile, to a hollow tree in his village, Meliandou. The team discovered that Emile and other children frequently played in this tree, which housed a large colony of free-tailed bats; the scientists believe Emile was exposed to the virus through contact with the bats and their droppings. While the bats tested negative for active Ebola infection, the study suggests the virus may persist in bat colonies, highlighting the need for coexistence rather than culling to prevent future outbreaks.

Stuart Bingham, the 2015 World Snooker Champion, is hoping to compete in this year's tournament but faces a dilemma regarding his first-round match against Joe Perry, as his wife is currently pregnant. The 39-year-old told BBC Essex that he would only play if she gives birth before the game on Monday, joking that he would need to "pot some balls and hurry up" if she goes into labor during the match. While his wife is supportive of him playing, Bingham admits they are still discussing the situation, unsure if the birth will happen before his first-round

The council voted to remove a dangerous section of a Grade II pier to the seaward end due to collapse risks. Work, expected to last three weeks and cost up to £650,000, will involve saving and storing salvageable parts of the structure.

The £21.5m Castle Mill development at Port Meadow has sparked legal action from the Campaign to Protect Rural England (CPRE), who argue Oxford City Council failed to conduct an environmental impact assessment before approving the five-storey student blocks. CPRE is seeking a judicial review to halt the project, claiming the buildings' height and design will irreparably damage the historic skyline and a protected Site of Special Scientific Interest, while the University of Oxford maintains it has mitigation plans in place and intends to complete the development as scheduled for the new academic year.

The Olympus Trust, which runs schools near Bristol, has warned it is at "crisis point" due to government funding cuts, threatening to shorten the school day and cut staff. Parents and unions have condemned the proposals as "diabolical" and "terrible," arguing they will negatively impact support for pupils, while the government maintains its new funding plans will increase budgets by 2.4%.

Experts warn that designating forest reserves in Liberia and the Democratic Republic of Congo to curb carbon emissions could displace up to 1.3 million people, as protected areas often remove indigenous communities who have lived on and protected the land for generations. Researchers argue that recognizing indigenous land rights is not only more just but more effective, as these communities actively protect forests and store more carbon per hectare than traditional protected areas. The study highlights a critical tension between international climate funding and local rights, cautioning that expanding protected areas without respecting these rights could trigger violent conflict and massive displacement.

A human skull was discovered near a roundabout in Telford, with police confirming it belonged to an adult male and had been there for at least two years. Further skeletal remains were found nearby, and the investigation is ongoing with forensic examinations and potential archaeological assistance.

Dusmatov secured a unanimous points victory to claim the gold medal, while Martinez made history as Colombia's first Olympic boxing finalist. Meanwhile, Hernandez and Argilagos both earned bronze medals after losing in the semi-finals.

University and College Union members are balloting on strike action after rejecting a 1.1% pay offer, which they describe as an insult given that vice-chancellors received a 5% rise. The unions argue that staff have suffered a real-terms pay cut of 14% since 2009, and are prepared to take industrial action in the autumn unless employers improve the offer.

The Scottish government has intervened in East Dunbartonshire Council's proposal to close St Joseph's Primary in Milngavie, citing concerns over inaccurate information in the consultation process. While the council plans to merge St Joseph's with St Andrew's Primary in Bearsden into a new £9 million building, the government's review highlights procedural flaws and unaddressed concerns from Education Scotland. Despite this setback, the council remains committed to the merger to meet budget savings targets, while a separate plan to close two Kirkintilloch primaries and build a new £7 million school is set to

Kazuyoshi Miura, known as "King Kazu," has signed a contract extension with his second-division club that will keep him playing past his 49th birthday, making his professional career span over 30 years. The 55-year-old veteran, who began his career in Brazil at age 15, remains motivated to contribute everything he has, holding the record as Japan's oldest scorer while aiming to continue his remarkable longevity in the sport.

Security forces used tear gas against protesters in Indian-administered Kashmir, while shelling across the Line of Control killed seven people. The violence was sparked by the anniversary of Burhan Wani's death, which led to restrictions and internet blackouts in the region.

A "Leave" vote in the Brexit referendum was anticipated to cause significant financial market disturbances, prompting central banks to prepare emergency measures to ensure stability. Authorities are ready to provide liquidity to banks facing inter-market borrowing difficulties and to intervene in currency markets to stabilize exchange rates, particularly for the British pound and Swiss franc. These actions include using swap lines and foreign currency reserves to prevent a freeze in the financial system.

The 33-year-old back-row forward, who joined Sale in 2011 after six years at Northampton, is departing the club to pursue a teaching career at Wrekin College. Having won the European Challenge Cup with Saints and made a Champions Cup final, he leaves on his own terms after enjoying a successful tenure. He will play his final game for Sale at Newcastle on Saturday before beginning his new role.

Tawel Fan ward at Glan Clwyd Hospital was closed over three years ago after reports of patients being treated like animals, with at least seven families told treatment may have contributed to their deaths. An independent investigation by the Health and Social Care Advisory Service is ongoing to determine if care quality was a contributory factor, though a mortality review remains unpublished despite being completed. The health board remains in special measures costing £5m annually as the scandal continues to erode public trust.

Declan Paul Butcher was sentenced to 14 months in prison for two unprovoked "single punch" assaults on Market Street in Limavady in October 2014. CCTV footage showed him knocking one man unconscious and fracturing the jaw of a second man who tried to help. The judge condemned Butcher for inflicting "gratuitous violence" on "completely innocent" members of the public.

Jill Ellis stated that Hope Solo's poor decision has negatively impacted US Soccer ahead of the Women's World Cup, following her domestic violence charges being dropped and a positive drug test from 2012. Solo will miss upcoming friendlies against France and England after tweeting she needs to "decompress" from recent stress, while her husband was arrested for DUI in a separate incident.

Three employees and a former employee of The Johnson Partnership in Nottingham have pleaded guilty to conspiracy to supply cocaine between October and December last year. The group, including Omar Khan, are due to be sentenced on 15 April after the court heard the case involved the recovery of 1kg of the Class A drug.

British Transport Police have authorized the deployment of Tasers to officers in Scotland, citing the "severe" terrorism threat as justification. The move brings Scotland in line with England, where the weapons have been used since 2011, and is described as a "proportionate response" to protect both the public and officers.

ID Systems, an industrial and commercial utilities company based in Glasgow, is expanding its workforce by creating new jobs in Lanarkshire, backed by a £1.5 million investment from UKSE (Tata Steel's subsidiary). The funding will support the company's growth strategy following a major contract win, enabling the creation of a new senior management team and facilitating a significant increase in staff to meet rising demand.

A Brazilian football team, Chapecoense, was involved in a fatal crash in Colombia that killed 71 people, including most of the squad and staff. Five survivors, including defender Helio Hermito Zampier Neto and goalkeeper Jakson Ragnar Follmann, are currently receiving medical treatment, with the pilot reportedly running out of fuel after missing a refuelling stop. Colombian and Bolivian authorities are investigating the crash, with evidence suggesting the plane lacked sufficient fuel for the journey to Medellin.

The 70-year-old Time Team presenter joined anti-tunnel campaigners to argue that the A303 plans threaten the wider archaeological landscape of Stonehenge. He criticized the proposed 1.8-mile tunnel as "old-fashioned," suggesting a longer alternative to better protect the site's significance. Highways England maintains the project will improve journey times and protect the World Heritage Site, but the Stonehenge Alliance insists other traffic-reduction options should be explored.

Everton secured a 4-0 victory over Wolfsburg to top Group H in the Europa League, with goals from a Ricardo Rodriguez own goal, Seamus Coleman, Leighton Baines' penalty, and Kevin Mirallas. The win was a statement of intent from manager Roberto Martinez, who fielded a strong side to prove the club's commitment to the competition after missing out on the Champions League last season. The result gives Everton confidence to progress from a group that also includes Lille and Krasnodar.

After joining Blackpool in 2013 and making 119 league appearances, the 35-year-old helped the team finish third this season before losing to Millwall in the play-off semi-finals. He expressed disappointment at the season's end, feeling there was "unfinished business" following their near-miss.

Pawel Sroka, 33, has been charged with the murder of his partner, Joanna Trojniak, 29, following a post-mortem examination that confirmed she died from a stab wound to the chest. Sroka is due to appear at Bromley Magistrates' Court on 4 April, while Ms. Trojniak's next of kin have been informed.

Prostate cancer is the fourth leading cause of cancer death in men, yet it remains under-researched and overlooked, often referred to as "the Cinderella cancer." Researchers at Cambridge are working to improve radiotherapy precision and reduce side effects, while a major genetic study has identified 80 new markers that could lead to better screening and earlier diagnosis.

Worcester secured a 31-28 victory over Wasps, moving them out of the relegation zone and guaranteeing a play-off spot for Wasps. The match was defined by Wasps' Bryce Heem being sent off for a tackle on Le Roux, which allowed Worcester to capitalize with two late tries. Despite the numerical disadvantage, Wasps fought back but ultimately fell short, with Worcester's defense and kicking game proving decisive.

French President Francois Hollande expressed "deep sadness" over the death of Huguette Dupeu, while a huge march against terrorism is planned for Sunday in Tunis. The attack, claimed by Islamic State, was the deadliest since the 2011 uprising, leading the Prime Minister to dismiss six police chiefs and admit security shortcomings.

Stratfor's satellite imagery reveals that ISIS has systematically destroyed Mosul airport's runways and infrastructure to deny Iraqi forces a critical logistical asset, rendering the site nearly unusable for approaching troops. The destruction, which mirrors the group's tactics at Qayyarah air base, serves both to clear defensive sightlines and make repair efforts significantly more difficult than at previous sites. While the sugar factory remains intact as a testament to ISIS's utility, the group's scorched-earth strategy at Mosul airport represents a major setback for coalition forces attempting to reclaim the city.

Network Rail is carrying out major engineering work over the Easter break to complete the Reading station redevelopment and other projects, but has warned that the risk of overruns remains high. To mitigate potential delays, hundreds of buses are on standby, and the closures follow previous disruptions at King's Cross and Paddington where works overran.

Plans were approved for Coastal Oil and Gas Limited to drill at St Nicholas, though the permit explicitly bans hydraulic fracturing. Natural Resources Wales approved the exploratory work following a thorough assessment, but emphasized that fracking remains subject to a temporary ban pending devolved decision-making powers. The company must complete all work and land reinstatement within 12 months, with the Welsh government preferring to focus on renewable energy over the "unproven" fracking technology.

Amazon is moving its European tax registration from Luxembourg to the UK, Germany, Spain, and Italy, ending a low-tax arrangement that had drawn heavy criticism. The company stated this shift, which began over two years ago, ensures sales made through local subsidiaries are now recorded in the countries where the customers are located. Additionally, Amazon is working to establish a branch in France, while the European Union intensifies investigations into similar tax deals by other tech giants like Apple and Starbucks.

Junior doctors in England have begun strike action over pay and working conditions, with the British Medical Association (BMA) arguing that current contracts are outdated and unfair. The walkouts, which started on November 8th and are set to continue into next year, come after negotiations between the BMA and the government failed to reach a resolution. While the government has indicated it will impose a new contract next year, the BMA has vowed to continue industrial action to protect junior doctors' rights.

The 19-year-old will be eligible to play for Oxford United in the Football League Trophy final against Barnsley on Sunday after joining the England Under-20 squad over Easter. Manager Michael Appleton praised the player's strong form and bright future, noting he is "highly thought of" at Goodison Park.

Kingston Maurward College received £3.24m for a new animal sciences building, while Weymouth College was awarded £0.5m to refurbish two buildings. These grants are part of a £214m investment in 47 colleges across England, aimed at ensuring "first rate facilities" and supporting the government's new skills strategy.

Greg Dyke has invited the family of former West Bromwich Albion forward Jeff Astle to Wembley Stadium to discuss the risks of heading footballs, following new evidence that he died from a brain condition linked to boxing rather than Alzheimer's. The family has long campaigned for research into the long-term effects of head injuries in football, and the meeting aims to address player education and medical policies regarding concussions.

The article explores the growing wealth gap between the world's top 1% and the rest of society, noting that while the threshold for "serious wealth" is around $100 million, the divide has widened since the 2008 financial crisis. Robert Kuhn, a member of the wealthy elite, acknowledges that public hostility toward the rich is "justified" due to increased awareness via the internet, but argues that limiting wealth inheritance is necessary to maintain social mobility. Despite global improvements in living standards, the OECD reports that income inequality in most developed nations is at its widest level

The 18-year-old identical twins have made nine Premiership appearances this season, becoming only the fourth set of twins to play together in the league's history. Both feature in the back row and have represented England at Under-20 level, with Steve Diamond highlighting them as key to the club's academy development plans.

Police are appealing for witnesses after a man was seen near Corbett Place and Calais View at around 8:30 AM on Thursday. The suspect is described as being in his late teens or early 20s, approximately 5ft 9in tall, with dark curly short hair and a dark top.

The US, UK, and Canada blocked an Egypt-backed proposal to hold a regional forum that might have forced Israel to acknowledge its nuclear capabilities. Analysts suggest the move was intended to pressure Israel, which neither confirms nor denies possessing nuclear weapons, into making its status public. The failure of the talks means the next review conference will not take place until 2020 at the earliest.

The UK government is pushing to accelerate fracking development, with Energy Secretary Amber Rudd urging councils in England to approve applications within 16 weeks. However, this move contradicts the Welsh Government's stance, as Natural Resources Minister Carl Sargeant reiterated that the fracking moratorium remains in place in Wales, prioritizing renewable energy instead. The divergence highlights a split between the UK government's support for fossil fuel extraction and Wales' commitment to sustainable, low-carbon energy sources.

Since dethroning Wladimir Klitschko, Tyson Fury has been driving a "runaway lorry," recklessly abandoning his titles and struggling with mental health issues. His recent withdrawal from the Klitschko rematch due to depression highlights a pattern of self-sabotage that mirrors other champions who lose focus after reaching the pinnacle of their sport.

Premiership boss Dai Young expects several Wasps players to be selected in Eddie Jones' England squad, with Guy Thompson and Sam Jones impressing at open-side flanker. However, concerns remain over the fitness of key players like James Haskell and Jack Clifford, while youngster Will Evans is set to be named in the England Performance Squad despite his director of rugby insisting he is not yet ready for Test rugby.

The exhibition "From Dark to Light" at The Old Low Light Heritage Centre showcases the work of Victor Noble Rainbird, a North Shields artist whose career was largely overlooked until now. Featuring a large collection of his paintings—many unseen in public—it highlights his focus on the North Sea and hometown life, while also presenting his poignant wartime drawings from the Western Front. The show runs from July 10 to September 6 and aims to reframe Rainbird's legacy as both a "much misunderstood artist" and a remarkable chronicler of North East history.

Scott Brown's return to the Scotland squad is almost certain for the World Cup qualifier against England, with manager Gordon Strachan set to benefit from the midfielder's leadership and form. Brendan Rodgers' former Celtic boss Neil Lennon believes Brown's decision to return was premature, noting the 31-year-old is playing well and could be the "jag" Scotland need to secure a win. Mark McGhee also highlighted that Brown's presence would make the rest of the squad better, suggesting his recall strengthens Scotland's chances ahead of the Wembley clash.

A buzzard became trapped in a wire fence in Bethesda while chasing a wood pigeon. RSPCA Inspector Mike Pugh successfully freed the bird, remarking that it was feisty but unharmed, and released it back into the wild immediately.

The Communication Workers Union announced a walkout starting Monday, December 19, including Christmas Eve, involving thousands of Crown Post Office workers. Despite the strike, the Post Office stated that "at least" 97% of its 11,600 branches would remain open, calling the action "extremely disappointed" while agreeing to resume talks on Wednesday.

Mike Nesbitt launched the Ulster Unionist manifesto, framing the election as a referendum on the Renewable Heat Incentive scandal and the current Stormont leadership. He emphasized the need for partnership over domination, while clarifying his desire to work with the SDLP rather than Sinn Féin if given the choice. Despite controversy over his comments, Nesbitt stood by his remarks and focused on the party's platform addressing health, policing, and Brexit concerns.

Irish police, customs, and the Health Products Regulatory Authority seized over 60,000 vials of anabolic steroids, along with human growth hormones and erectile dysfunction pills, during raids in Muff and Lifford. A man in his 30s was arrested but released without charge, while authorities confirmed evidence of an illegal manufacturing operation had been discovered.

Taoiseach Enda Kenny suggested that Brexit could trigger a future referendum on Irish unity if there is clear evidence of a majority wanting to leave the UK, a notion dismissed by unionist politicians as "mischievous" and "much ado about nothing." Sinn Féin called for unity discussions, arguing the EU exit creates a "greater opportunity," while unionists insisted the Secretary of State had ruled out such a poll and that Kenny's comments were politically motivated given his impending departure.

Morecambe have started the season strongly, winning three consecutive league games to top the table, highlighted by Kevin Ellison's goal in the 1-0 victory over Yeovil. Manager Bentley praised the squad's unity and veteran Ellison's professionalism, emphasizing the need to remain grounded despite the early success.

Qatar has rejected a 13-point ultimatum from Saudi Arabia and its allies, which demands the closure of Al Jazeera and a reduction in ties with Iran. The U.S. Secretary of State has called the demands "reasonable," but Qatar argues they are an attempt to limit its sovereignty rather than combat terrorism. The crisis has intensified with warnings of a "parting of ways" if Qatar fails to comply, while the U.S. and Qatar maintain that dialogue is necessary to resolve the dispute.

Suspended UKIP member Suzanne Evans was barred from running in the party's leadership contest due to a six-month ban she claims was politically motivated, stating she was prevented by "a handful of people at the top." Despite this, she endorsed fellow councillor Lisa Duffy as the "best chance" for UKIP to reform and move toward the political centre.

Delhi banned Uber and other web-based taxi firms after a 26-year-old woman was raped by a driver she booked via the app; police say the driver confessed to the crime. The incident adds to a rising trend of sexual violence in India, highlighted by recent cases including the kidnapping of a Japanese student and the arrest of two policemen for raping a teenager.

Wales' remarkable Euro 2016 campaign ended in a semi-final defeat to Portugal, but their "Red Wall" of supporters celebrated the team's unprecedented success. The tournament served as a breakthrough for Welsh football, shattering a 58-year absence from major events and fostering a deep bond between the players and fans. Despite the loss, the experience was defined by a shared sense of achievement and the belief that Wales had finally joined football's elite.

Renfrewshire Council has stated that a long-term plan to improve local fortunes is already underway, noting that the latest deprivation figures are based on data from last year and do not fully reflect recent efforts. Despite this, Glasgow has 56 of the 100 most deprived areas, while Edinburgh has six, and the Scottish government has warned that deep-seated inequalities remain a significant challenge requiring continued political action.

British rowers Cassells and Scrimgeour won the lightweight men's double sculls title at the Rotterdam championships, clocking 6:29.63 to finish ahead of Denmark and China. Meanwhile, Ireland's Paul O'Donovan advanced to the lightweight single sculls final with a strong semi-final win, while Irish duo Mark O'Donovan and Shane O'Driscoll qualified for the lightweight pairs final in second place.

Kilmarnock defender Craig Barr and striker Mark Stewart have joined Scottish Championship side Kirkcaldy, alongside new signing Johnston, who previously played for Kilmarnock. The trio bring experience to the club, with Barr and Stewart having previously featured for Rovers last season.

Liverpool came from behind to defeat Swansea 3-1, moving back to within a point of the Premier League's top four. Roberto Firmino and James Milner scored either side of half-time to secure the win, while Leroy Fer had given the hosts an early lead from a corner. The victory extends Liverpool's winning streak to four games, but leaves Swansea's manager Francesco Guidolin under increasing pressure amid their ongoing battle against relegation.

The article highlights the first positive steroid test in Scottish rugby history, focusing on Sam Chalmers, who claimed he obtained the substances online. It argues that while players face pressure to bulk up, using artificial aids constitutes cheating, and notes that roughly 1.36% of elite players have been caught doping, suggesting the issue may be more prevalent in lower leagues.

TRNSMT, held at Glasgow Green this weekend, features headliners Radiohead, Kasabian, and Biffy Clyro across three stages. The festival replaces the cancelled T in the Park and will have tight security following recent terror attacks, with strict bans on drugs and pyrotechnics.

North Korea has officially confirmed the restart of operations at the Yongbyon nuclear reactor, a move that could accelerate its plutonium production for nuclear weapons. The White House and international community have condemned the action, reiterating that North Korea must fulfill its obligations and warning it will not be accepted as a nuclear state. This development, occurring amid heightened regional tensions, marks a significant setback for the stalled six-party talks aimed at denuclearizing the Korean Peninsula.

Cambridgeshire Police reopened a murder investigation into the 1990 disappearance of Andrew Bedford after discovering human bones at a Ramsey garage. A 64-year-old man from Ramsey has been arrested, and detectives believe Bedford was shot with a shotgun during the evening of September 28. The remains will undergo DNA testing to help bring resolution to his family.

Salford City Reds owner Dr Marwan Koukash is aggressively reshaping the club with bold signings and a push to raise the salary cap, aiming to make Salford the country's biggest rugby league team within three to four years. While he has secured the interest of high-profile coaches like Brian Noble, the ambitious plans face uncertainty over funding and the sport's current financial climate.

Ireland secured a perfect 3-0 record in the ICC Women's World Twenty20 Qualifier by dismissing Zimbabwe for just 78 and chasing the target with seven balls to spare. Isobel Joyce's four wickets and a strong opening partnership between Cecilia Joyce and Clare Shillington paved the way for the victory. A win against Scotland on Thursday will guarantee Ireland a spot in next year's World Twenty20 in India.

Colchester Hospital was rated "inadequate" by the Care Quality Commission, which found it relies on "unsuitable" agency staff and demonstrated "poor leadership" with "only a limited capacity to improve." The trust, which has been in special measures since 2013, was told it must submit weekly improvement plans to exit those measures, though the chief executive admitted the hospital's biggest challenge is reducing its dependency on agency workers.

Mark Cavendish finished sixth in the scratch race and seventh in the elimination race at the Olympic track cycling, while Becky James broke the women's sprint Olympic record and advanced to the quarter-finals.

Finance Minister Máirtín Ó Muilleoir announced a reallocation of £200 million to health services in 2016/17, bringing the total additional funding allocated this year to £200 million. The money will primarily target unscheduled care, including emergency departments and addressing bed blocking within hospitals. Additionally, £30 million was redirected to schools and roads maintenance, while the finance minister confirmed no new spending cuts were implemented despite budget pressures.

The Winklevoss twins have filed a new lawsuit against Facebook, claiming the company suppressed evidence during their previous legal battle over the site's creation. This comes after they previously tried to reopen a 2008 settlement, which a court ruled they must accept, but they are now alleging Mark Zuckerberg hid crucial documents regarding his relationship with the brothers while at Harvard.
A teenage pedestrian was struck by a Ford Focus in Oldgate Lane, Rotherham, on Saturday. The driver was unharmed, and police are appealing for witnesses to come forward.

Harry Chapman Pincher, a former defence correspondent for the Daily Express, became renowned for his investigative journalism and ability to recall minute details without taking notes. After retiring, he authored books alleging that Britain's security services had been penetrated by top-level spies. His unorthodox methods, including cultivating sources over lunch at a French restaurant bugged by MI5 and the KGB, allowed him to expose sensitive information about Britain's atomic weapons programme and high-level government secrets.

Dundee forward Stewart has agreed to join Birmingham City, passing his medical after previously rejecting a move. The 25-year-old, who scored six goals in three games this season, could make his Championship debut against Leeds on Saturday, becoming the club's second signing of the week following Che Adams' arrival.

A former private in her 20s accepted a conditional caution for misconduct in a public office after being arrested in connection with Operation Elveden. As part of the agreement, she paid £40 to an armed forces charity, avoiding prosecution while acknowledging her responsibility for the offence.

The Care Inspectorate gave Nithsdale House in Glasgow a score of one (unsatisfactory) across three areas, noting "very little progress" since a previous inspection and poor medication practices. Similarly, Drumpellier Lodge in Bargeddie received the second lowest rating of two (weak), with inspectors finding that 10 previous improvement requirements remained unmet.

Police were called to Derby Road in Enfield after reports of a gun in a car. The vehicle was stopped at 16:00 GMT, and four men were arrested and are currently being held at a north London police station.

A power outage affecting over 53,000 customers in Lancaster, Morecambe, and Carnforth began at 11:00 BST and was fully restored by 16:30 BST. The cause remains unknown, though a similar flood in 2015 had previously caused a blackout, and the disruption impacted traffic lights, schools, and businesses across the region.

The High Court quashed Sajid Javid's refusal of a development plan for Hatchfield Farm in Newmarket, ruling his decision was "plainly deficient" and inconsistent. The judge ordered a reconsideration, emphasizing the need for housing growth in the area and noting the secretary of state had failed to properly apply planning guidelines.

The Isle of Wight Council has made the Cowes crossing free until July 2nd to address public frustration over the new ferry's repeated breakdowns and groundings. Council leaders have ordered an audit of the project, acknowledging it has been a "frustrating and disappointing start" since its launch in May. While compensation for damaged cars and local businesses is under discussion, officials maintain the issues are temporary "teething problems" of a prototype vessel.

Tunisia international Sliti has signed a three-year contract with Lille after joining on loan last summer, having made just five appearances since the African Cup of Nations. The 24-year-old, who previously played for Paris FC, has featured 16 times for the club, scoring once during their 4-2 win over Caen.
British astronaut Tim Peake spoke to schoolchildren from the International Space Station, sharing experiments and his experiences during his six-week mission.

Martyn Irvine made history by becoming the first Irish cyclist in 117 years to win a world track title, adding a silver in the points race at the World Championships in Belarus. Despite suffering a fractured hip in Taiwan shortly after, he remarkably regained fitness to win European bronze and a World Cup event in Manchester, earning him the BBC Northern Ireland Sports Personality of the Year award.

A major emergency was declared at Prestwick Airport after an Italian C-27J aircraft lost communication and was escorted by RAF Typhoons from Lossiemouth. The plane landed safely around 8:00 PM, and while Scottish airspace remained open, the incident caused brief flight delays at Glasgow and Edinburgh airports.

West Midlands Police arrested five men aged 18 to 37 on suspicion of terrorism-related offenses following the discovery of suspect devices in Birmingham's Lee Bank area. The suspects, detained in Stoke-on-Trent and Birmingham, are currently being held for up to seven more days as detectives from the Counter Terrorism Unit seek further detention.

The 2016 European Championship kicks off on June 10 with 24 teams competing for the first time, featuring England and Wales making their debuts alongside established powers like Germany and Spain. France, the hosts and bookmakers' favorites, will aim to replicate their 1998 World Cup success despite the absence of Karim Benzema, while the tournament structure means the top two teams and four best third-placed sides progress to the last 16.

Great Britain will face Greece in a home game at the Copper Box on July 23rd, seeking revenge after a 92-64 defeat in Patras earlier this month. The match serves as Britain's final warm-up before FIBA EuroBasket 2017, with guard Teddy Okereafor expecting a great atmosphere ahead of the tournament in Istanbul.

Wales suffered an 11th consecutive defeat to Australia, losing 23-18 despite the Wallabies being reduced to 13 men for seven minutes in the second half. A lack of composure and heroic Australian defence, including a try-saving tackle by Ben McCalman, repelled Wales' chances, with fly-half Bernard Foley kicking the decisive penalties to secure Australia's quarter-final spot.

Scotland coach Cotter will depart at season's end to be replaced by Glasgow's Gregor Townsend. Strauss says the squad wants to give Cotter a strong send-off ahead of a tough opening match against Ireland, who are heavy favorites having won 14 of the last 17 Six Nations clashes.

Retired General David Petraeus warns that "industrial-strength" extremists like IS cannot be defeated by military force alone, emphasizing the need for a political solution and Sunni support to stabilize Iraq. He views the recent loss of Ramadi as a significant setback but remains confident the city will be retaken quickly, while stressing that the Iraqi military must refine its strategy to ultimately succeed against the group.

A hacker attack on the City of Edinburgh Council's website service provider, based in England, occurred 10 days ago. The council has assured affected individuals that only email addresses were accessed and that no other personal data was compromised. Officials have reported the incident to authorities and are contacting those impacted to offer support and advice regarding potential phishing risks.

A joint operations room was formed by rebel groups in response to increased attacks on residential areas and displaced people, launching offensives in Latakia and Hama. This escalation has led the Syrian opposition to consider suspending peace talks in Geneva, fearing the seven-week ceasefire is collapsing around key front lines like Aleppo.

Instagram is set to introduce ads in a few months to transform into a sustainable business, following its acquisition by Facebook for $1 billion. The company, which has 150 million users, has struggled to monetize its platform without alienating its community, having previously faced backlash over proposed changes to image ownership terms. With social media advertising booming, Instagram aims to capture a larger share of the market, mirroring Facebook's success in boosting mobile ad revenues.

The Mercury Prize shortlist features David Bowie's final album, Blackstar, alongside Radiohead's A Moon Shaped Pool and nominees like The 1975 and Kano. The winner will be chosen by a public vote and a panel of judges, with the ceremony taking place at the Hammersmith Apollo on September 15th.

Gurpal Virdi, a 56-year-old retired detective from west London, was acquitted of indecently assaulting a prisoner and misconduct in public office. He had claimed the Metropolitan Police pursued the charges as part of a 17-year campaign following his testimony about racism during the Stephen Lawrence inquiry. The retired officer, who served for 30 years before retiring in 2012, maintained his innocence throughout the trial at Southwark Crown Court.

The UK government is under pressure to reconsider its "hard Brexit" approach, with former ministers arguing that staying in the single market is necessary to maintain cross-party consensus. Despite the election result, Welsh and UK politicians are urging Theresa May to pursue a flexible strategy that allows businesses to trade freely while leaving the EU legally.

Hillsborough families met with Home Secretary Theresa May to discuss the aftermath of the inquests, which concluded fans were unlawfully killed. The talks focused on the conduct of South Yorkshire Police and the implementation of a "Hillsborough Law" to improve cooperation with investigations. May pledged to ensure families' voices were heard as they await potential criminal prosecutions.

The Crown Prosecution Service has issued new guidance stating that online harassment, or "virtual mobbing," will be prosecuted as severely as offline offenses. Director Alison Saunders emphasized that while the internet is not an anonymous space, context remains vital to ensure free speech is not stifled. The guidance aims to help police identify and act on online crimes, including "doxxing," more effectively.

Faizan, a young boy, was killed during protests against Indian rule near a polling station in Srinagar, where he was struck by a bullet while trying to understand the commotion. His death, captured on mobile phone videos, became part of a day that saw eight people killed and a historically low voter turnout of 7.1%. The incident highlights the volatile security situation in the region, with paramilitary forces deployed to secure elections faced with stone-pelting protesters.

North Wales Police were called to a crash involving a silver Ford Transit truck in Talysarn, Gwynedd, on Friday afternoon. A woman was airlifted to hospital but later died, and police are now appealing for witnesses to the incident.

Four bidders—Abellio, Arriva, KeolisAmey, and MTR—have submitted proposals for the new Wales and Borders rail franchise, with the winner to be selected in early 2018. The successful bidder will be required to reinvest a portion of its profits into the railway and deliver major upgrades to the network, particularly around Cardiff as part of the Metro scheme. The Welsh Government aims to establish an "ambitious and creative not for profit model" that prioritizes increased passenger numbers and integrated public transport across the region.

Robbie Shepherd, the 80-year-old broadcasting legend and champion of the Doric dialect, is stepping down as the permanent host of the long-running Scottish music show "Take the Floor" after more than 35 years. Known for his distinctive voice and deep knowledge of traditional Scottish music, Shepherd will present his final programme this weekend before passing the baton to younger presenter Gary Innes. Despite his retirement from the regular show, he plans to continue with one-off broadcasts, leaving behind a legacy as one of Scotland's most recognizable voices in broadcasting.

Carlisle United have played three "home" fixtures at neutral grounds following flooding at Brunton Park, a situation that has drawn criticism from Stanley, who argues it creates an unfair advantage. He contends that while he sympathizes with the flooding victims, the league's handling of the postponements is inequitable for the other teams forced to travel to Carlisle. Despite his objections, the Cumbrians are set to continue playing at Blackburn's Ewood Park and Blackpool's Bloomfield Road.

Two Manchester United supporters were found inside Old Trafford stadium on Saturday morning after cutting themselves off from their tour group. Police were called but decided not to arrest the pair, who had been searched and passed through metal detectors earlier. The incident comes six months after a false alarm at a previous United game, when a suspect package was later revealed to be a fake explosive left from a training exercise.

Accrington Stanley overturned a two-goal deficit to defeat Preston North End 3-2 in the EFL Cup, with Billy Kee scoring a stoppage-time winner. The League Two side had earlier equalized through Jordan Hugill, but a late corner led to Kee's decisive header. The victory marks the second successive year Accrington have knocked out higher-league opposition in the competition.

Andrew Bickel had his tools stolen from a Cardiff charity shop but was reunited with them after a woman contacted him to say they had been left behind. The incident went viral, earning him media attention and offers to appear on television shows, which he found both surprising and amusing. He expressed relief that no one was left out of pocket and joked about being ready for his "five minutes of fame."

Scotland middle-distance runner Laura Muir will miss the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Australia to focus on completing her veterinary medicine degree, despite achieving a new personal best of 14:52.07 at the World Championships in London. Although she is "gutted" to miss the event, Muir prioritized her final year of university studies, noting that the Games' April dates conflict with her May exams. However, she remains focused on future targets, including the World Indoor Championships in March and potentially the Olympics.

Former Newcastle striker Nile Ranger was jailed for eight months in May for online banking fraud but is expected to return to training with Southend before the League One season starts on August 5. Manager Phil Brown stated that Ranger will need a week of training to regain match fitness, but acknowledged he likely won't be ready for the season opener. Ranger joined Southend in 2016 and scored eight goals in 27 league appearances last season.

Veteran broadcaster Sir Terry Wogan died of cancer at 77, leaving behind a legacy as "the absolute governor" of BBC Radio 2. His death was widely mourned, with tributes highlighting his charm, wit, and the deep connection he forged with listeners over a 50-year career.

Unions at BAE Systems have raised concerns about possible delays to the Royal Navy's new frigates, warning that work may not begin until 2017 and up to 800 jobs could be lost. However, Scottish Conservative leader Ruth Davidson insists the timetable remains unchanged, with the government confirming commitments to build eight Type 26 frigates on the Clyde. SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon has warned that breaking promises made during the referendum would be "seriously damaging" for the shipyards and the Scottish economy.

The Republican debate devolved into shouting matches and personal insults as Marco Rubio and Ted Cruz aggressively attacked frontrunner Donald Trump's business record and conservative credentials. With Trump winning three of the first four contests and Super Tuesday approaching, the other candidates are attempting to undermine his momentum, though their attacks may come too late to stop his path to the nomination.

Rother District Council has allocated £51,000 to fund beach patrols at Camber Sands following the deaths of seven men who drowned at the East Sussex beach last year. Councillor Sally-Ann Hart emphasized the need for the service to protect visitors and support the local tourism economy, while urging the public to be better informed about water safety. The council plans to have lifeguards on duty from late May through the summer holidays, pending the outcome of ongoing inquests.

Partick Thistle manager Osman is desperate to keep hold of assistant manager Archibald, who has been linked with other vacancies after guiding the team to a top-six finish last season. Osman praised Archibald as "one of the best managers I have played under," while teammate Adam Barton echoed the sentiment, stating his departure would be "personally disappointing." However, the club faces the potential loss of centre-back Liam Lindsay, who has traveled to Barnsley for a medical following an agreed fee.

Ten individuals were detained at Montreal's Trudeau International Airport over the weekend and had their passports confiscated, though police have not charged them. The families of the suspects have been informed that the decision to leave the country was made by a single family member, leaving relatives distressed and unable to understand the situation. Canadian authorities are investigating the arrests in the context of the ongoing global terror threat and the country's military mission against IS militants in Iraq and Syria.

An independent report commissioned by the Department of Health estimates that groups including health tourists and expats cost the NHS £2 billion annually. The government aims to save £500 million a year by deterring health tourism and levying non-European temporary residents, though critics argue doctors should not act as border guards. Health Secretary Jeremy Hunt maintains that while emergency care remains free, the NHS must ensure foreign visitors make a "fair contribution" to its sustainability.

Belfast Giants secured a 5-3 victory over Cardiff Devils, with Colin Shields and Scott Aarssen trading goals in a fast-paced first period before Ryan Martinelli and Mark Garside extended the lead in the second. Alex Foster and Steve Saviano added late goals to seal the win, leaving Belfast top of the table with a game in hand as the festive schedule continues.

After a decade of restoration, a historic steam engine built in Doncaster is set to return to the East Coast mainline. The locomotive, named after the Edinburgh to London service it once ran, will make its first journey in ten years, celebrating its status as an icon of British engineering.

A group of 249 men are suing the Catholic Church over historical sexual abuse at St William's residential school, with only one of the initial five cases resulting in a compensation award. In December, a judge ruled in favor of one claimant, ordering the church to pay £14,000 in damages, while dismissing three others. The former head of the school and a co-defendant have been jailed for abuse, and the De La Salle Brothers have apologized unreservedly, with another round of claims expected in late 2017.
